current_determination: R60 corrects the quantifier structure of the coupling-window obligation. With the native inverse-square recursion x_j=g_j^{-2}=x_{j-1}-beta_j, positive beta drift makes the effective coupling grow toward coarser scales. Therefore one fixed bare coupling cannot be the all-depth UV target. Under an upper beta corridor 0<=beta_j<=b_+, fixed-depth persistence through N steps follows from g_0<=(gamma^{-2}+N b_+)^{-1/2}. Under a positive two-sided corridor and a fixed weak endpoint, the tuned bare coupling necessarily scales as g_0^(N)~N^{-1/2}. The live global object is therefore an N-dependent TunedUVWeakCouplingTrajectory, not FixedBareCouplingAllDepthPersistence. Exact CMP109 equations (0.18),(0.20), inequalities (1.0.33), beta constants and error terms remain source-unextracted and are not reconstructed from modern secondary claims. The published Balaban spine located through CMP122-II still does not source-attest the missing second-order all-depth coupling-flow theorem; Dimock [81] independently corroborates that historical publication boundary.
major_new_results: FixedBareCouplingAllDepthPersistence is retyped as the wrong target for an asymptotically free UV construction.
For prescribed depth N, an upper beta corridor yields the sufficient weak-window condition g_0<=(gamma^{-2}+N b_+)^{-1/2}.
With a positive two-sided beta corridor and fixed weak endpoint, the tuned bare sequence satisfies g_0^(N)~N^{-1/2}.
The canonical marginal-flow object is TunedUVWeakCouplingTrajectory: for each N choose g_0^(N)->0 so the whole N-step path stays in the CMP119/CMP122-II weak-coupling jurisdiction.
The N^{-1/2} scaling is a conditional derivation from a beta corridor, not promoted as the exact CMP109 theorem.
The published-source search found no later Bałaban spine item that can presently be attested as the missing second-order coupling-flow theorem.
